title: Surge insulation proxy for transient limiter outages and adaptive backpressure
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Transient outages in the central rate-limiter fleet cause sharp, system-wide availability and SLO regressions when upstream services either receive 503s or experience sudden, global throttles. Current fallbacks (global circuit-break to allow degraded capacity) either underutilize regional capacity or create unfair booking across tenants.

Goal: Implement a lightweight surge-insulation proxy layer colocated with edge ingress that: (1) quickly absorbs short-lived central limiter outages by performing conservative local admission, (2) exposes an adaptive backpressure signal to callers that preserves tenant fairness, and (3) provides safe automatic rehydration to full global quota once central limiter health is restored. The solution must preserve SLOs for high-priority customers while bounding cost and avoiding global cascading throttles.

Success criteria (measurable):
- During simulated central limiter outage windows (1s-60s), P95 tail latency for hosted API routes increases by <= 2x baseline and error rate increase limited to <= 0.5% for P0 customers.
- No tenant experiences more than a 30% delta in allowed throughput vs. baseline during an outage window when normalized by configured weights.
- Fast recovery: >90% of queued requests processed within 10s after central limiter healthy.
- Observability: new metrics for insulated-admit-rate, local-fallback-duration, unfairness-index, and emitted backpressure-level.

Design summary:
1) Surge-Insulation Proxy (SIP): a small module inserted at ingress proxies that maintains a compact, best-effort local admission state (soft credits) per tenant. Credits are seeded from the last known central quota and decay deterministically. SIP has three modes: Normal (stateless pass-through), Insulate (on central-limiter unavailability switch to local conservative admission), and Rehydrate (safe warm-up where we ramp admission as central signals capacity).
2) Adaptive Backpressure Signal: SIP returns a structured header and event (x-rw-backpressure: <level>) to callers when running in Insulate mode. Levels are numeric (0-5) and map to client-side retry/backoff guidance. We will document exact semantics for SDKs to implement polite backoff.
3) Fairness heuristic: local credits are distributed proportionally using weighted reservoir sampling across active tenants with additional short-term protection for recently-hit high-priority requests. This prevents starvation when short local caches are exhausted.
4) Circuit-break choreography: SIP subscribes to central-limiter health events (via health bus). On circuit open, proxies snapshot last known quotas, seed local credits, and begin Insulate mode. SIP also initiates a degraded telemetry stream to central so operators see per-region admission.Limits are conservatively tuned to avoid overruns that could break downstream SLOs.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Pros: avoids global SLA regressions to clients by keeping requests moving through local admission; smoother multi-region behavior; simpler rollout than full multi-master quota replication.
- Cons: local admission is best-effort and may allow short-term overconsumption of capacity; increases operational surface area and complexity in observability. We accept bounded overage risk and compensate with cost reconcilers.

Testing and simulation:
- Build a synthetic harness that can inject central-limiter failure modes (pause, delayed responses, misreports) and replay realistic traffic shapes (thundering-burst, fat-tail, steady-state).
- Run closed-loop chaos tests across two regions (us-west1, eu-central1) and verify fairness index and recovery times.
- Unit + integration tests for header signaling, credit decay math, and fair distribution algorithm.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Deploy SIP to 5% of ingress hosts in us-west1 with conservative credit caps and verbose telemetry.
- Phase 2 (regional): Expand to all hosts in one region and run chaos injection for central-limiter outages for 48h.
- Phase 3 (global): Gradual global rollout with A/B control comparing request success and billing deltas.

Observability & SLO mapping:
- New metrics: sip.mode, sip.local_admit_count, sip.local_reject_count, sip.unfairness_index, sip.rehydrate_rate.
- Dashboards: Per-region SLO impact, tenant fairness heatmap, admission delta vs central baseline.
- Alerts: sip.local_reject_rate > 1% for >5m, unfairness_index spikes > threshold, rehydrate failures >3 occurrences in 1h.

Operational playbooks:
- If central limiter is slow (increased latency) but healthy, flip SIP to 'probe' mode where it requests small quota slices; if error patterns worsen, switch to Insulate.
- Manual override to pin specific tenants to global-only enforcement when legal/compliance required.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting full consistent global quota replication.
- Not changing tenant billing model within this work (billing reconciliation handled by downstream process).
